title: Kelly's Irish family background and lack of musical ancestry
summary: Kelly says the family was theatrical and well educated but not musical; his grandparents came from Virginia and South Carolina to Mississippi around 1850.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, uh, I didn't get about the different Irish musicians in your family down, but, uh, quite pat. I don't know how many of them there were.

Uh, actually, I don't have much background as far as, uh, relatives, or ancestors who played music. Uh, the Irish part of my family were people who, uh, were kind of in the theater and, uh, interested in the arts. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.

Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Well educated, but no musical background. I told you of my great uncle Gus Clayton, who was a country peddler and a very good one. And that's about as much of a background as far as having inherited any talent or anything long as mine.
You don't remember the Irish people in the family singing any songs from the old country in particular, right?

No, we weren't quite that Irish because my mother was a country recipient. Yeah. And my grandfather and grandmother were all people from Virginia or South Carolina who had moved to Mississippi about 1850.

Yeah, I just wondered, because sometimes those things are kept alive. Well, it's only been, I think, in 77 that my mother would sing Scottish songs to me, which she had learned, I think, from her aunt. It was like that. People, sometimes immigrants were a little ashamed of things and were suppressed. I guess that's true. And just never did talk about them very much. Maybe they had good reason. I never did get the members of the Melody Four down pat either. Speaking of being Irish down pat. That's an unconscious bond that came out.
